newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul bourse ends at fifth consecutive 3-yr low.
newsitem.headline: Seoul bourse ends at fifth consecutive 3-yr low.

text.p: The Seoul bourse declined to its fifth consecutive three-year closing low on Tuesday, as nervous investors sold on the belief that there was no relief in sight, brokers said.
The composite stock index fell 10.57 points to a provisional close of 663.35. This was the lowest close since March 29, 1993, when the index ended at 652.21.

"Most people are very upset about the market and are getting a little panicked," said Casey Choe, a UBS Securities broker. "Many brokers feel the market will fall to 650 and some say as low as 620 before the floor is found."

Brokers said fundamental problems such as the uncertain economic outlook, high interest rates, and a floundering won made the stock market an unattractive proposition for many investors, especially foreigners.
Investors were particularly uninspired by the government's recent market boosting measures, they said.

"The market started better, but then people realised the market boosting measures weren't really going to improve the situation and started dumping," said Choi Tae-hwan, head of sales at KLB Securities.
The finance ministry said on Monday it would liberalise interest rates on customer deposits to within five percent from the fixed three percent at present.

Margin-loan maturity would be liberalised from the present three-month period and interest rates eased from 11 percent. The ministry also plans to boost stock buying by pension funds, but gave no details.
Some buying emerged in late trading for banks and securities shares, as these shares were seen as oversold, brokers said.
Commercial Bank of Korea rose 180 won to 5,180 and Kookmin Bank gained 200 won to 11,300. Daewoo Securities rose 300 won to 11,000.

Sammi Steel ended the day up 250 won to its upper limit of 3,420 after news that it was in talks to sell part of its stainless steel business to Pohang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO). POSCO was down 900 won to 35,700.
